subject: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?

messages.author: 2083d5dd75475d0e
messages.subject: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?
parts:
Hi all,

I'm looking for an efficient approach (perhaps one avoiding 'for' loops) to find the position (index) of the 4th "year" position for the first occurrence of 4 consecutive years below a certain value.

For example, given a time series of 16 years of abundance data in the vector 'z' below, the desired result would be 9, the index of the 4th "year" position for the first occurrence of 4 consecutive years < 100 -- this would mark a year of quasi-extinction. I don't have to worry about NA or other missing data issues.

z <- c(150, 150, 99, 99, 150, 99, 99, 99, 99, 150, 150, 99, 99, 99, 99, 100)

 Also, I've got an approach that works with for loops, but is ridiculously slow when I have to apply it to a large number of vectors. I'm happy to clarify if needed or share the slow code.

Many thanks in advance,
Patrick

messages.author: b35e99045f6c74c2
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?
parts:
Hi Patrick,

I would look into Rle(). It's pretty fast and useful for these types of tasks. For example:

> z < 100
 [1] FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE
[13]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE
> rle(z < 100)
Run Length Encoding
  lengths: int [1:7] 2 2 1 4 2 4 1
  values : logi [1:7] FALSE TRUE FALSE TRUE FALSE TRUE ...

You can access the length and value vectors with $lengths and $values. So maybe something like (I have't extensively checked this, be warned):

> rep(rle(z < 100)$lengths == 4, rle(z)$lengths)
 [1] FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE  TRUE
[13]  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE

and 

> which(rep(rle(z < 100)$lengths == 4, rle(z)$lengths))
[1]  6  7  8  9 12 13 14 15

> min(which(rep(rle(z < 100)$lengths == 4, rle(z)$lengths)))
[1] 6

But again — quick solution, haven't checked this extensively. Also, wouldn't the desired result be 6? Did I misunderstand the problem? 

V

Hey Patrick, 

The code below should be faster, not sure if it's fast enough for your needs.

i.low <- which(z < 100)
i.last <- i.low[1]
i.4 <- NA

counter <- 1
for( i in i.low[-1]){
  if(counter == 4) {
    i.4 <- i
    break
  }

  if(i-1 == i.last)
    counter = counter + 1
  i.last <- i
}

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Re: efficient approach to finding consecutive values in a vector?
parts:
Dear Ken and D-RUG,

Thank you for sending and fixing your approach. I think that it does the trick, but I haven't put it through the ringer test-wise.

For those interested, I opted to use Jaime's solution (see below) as I got it working first under the scenarios that I tested. I also worked on a version of the rle() approach working that Noam and Vince offered, but I recall that I had some issues getting it to work (both runs above and below the threshold value are tallied). I've included a quick example using functions for each approach, including my original version.

Sorry that I took a few weeks to report back to the group and many thanks to D-RUG for the help.

Thank you all -
Patrick

----------------------------------
# Here's an example using
set.seed(1)
runl <- 4
value <- 100
z <- rnorm(50, value, 10)


# The candidate functions
# Ken's solution
kenf(x=z, value = value, runl = runl)
# Jaime's solution
JA_consec(z, value = value, run_length = runl)
# The rle() approach from Noam and Vince [I wasn't able to catch all errors when I tested it]
vec_QE_count(z, run_length = runl, value = value)
# Patrick's original function
QE_counter(data = data.frame(z=z), value, runl)


# The functions:

# Ken's solution

kenf <- function(x, value = 100, runl = 4) {
  y <- which(x <  value)
  ans <- min(y[runl:length(y)][ y[runl:length(y)] - y[ 1:(length(y) -(runl-1)) ] == (runl -1)])
  return(ans)
}

kenf(x=z, value = value, runl = runl)

# Jaime's function
JA_consec <- function(z, value, run_length) {
 
  i.low <- which(z < value)
 
  i.last <- i.low[1]

counter <- 1
  for( i in i.low[-1]){

if(counter == run_length)  return(as.integer(i.last)) #  need the double to ensure that data.table gets what it expects
   
    if(i-1 == i.last)  counter <- counter + 1 else counter <- 1
   
    if(i == i.low[length(i.low)] & counter < run_length) i.last <- NA else i.last <- i
  }
  if (is.null(class(i.last))) print("error here")
  return(as.integer(i.last))
}

# rle approach Noam and Vince
# didn't get to work quite right

vec_QE_count <- function(z, run_length, value) {
  rl <- rle(z <= value)
  if (max(rl$length[which(rl$values == 1)]) >= run_length ) {  
    OUT <- sum(rl$length[1:(min(which(rl$length >= run_length & rl$values == 1))-1) ] ) + run_length
  } else {
    OUT <- NA # if no runs are at least 4
  }
  return(OUT)
}

vec_QE_count(z, run_length = runl, value = value)

# Finally, my original approach
QE_counter <- function(data, value, runl) {
 
  extInd <- vector("integer", ncol(data))
  for (h in 1:ncol(data)) { 
    qeInd <- which(data[,h] <= value)
    extRuns <- vector("integer", 0)
    k <- 1
    if (length(qeInd) >= runl) {
      for (i in 1:(length(qeInd)-3)) {
        if (qeInd[i] == (qeInd[i+1] - 1) & qeInd[i] == (qeInd[i+2] - 2) &
              qeInd[i] == (qeInd[i+3] - 3)  ) {
          extRuns[k] <- (qeInd[i] + 3)
          k <- k + 1
        } 
      }
    } else {
      extRuns[k] <- (nrow(data) + 1)
      k <- k+1
    }
    if(length(extRuns > 0)) extInd[h] <- min(extRuns) else extInd[h] <- NA
  }
  return(extInd)
} # end QE_count
